reason: The narrative depicts the regular people of Israel as naive and easily manipulated by Absalom, who systematically deceives them with flattery and false promises of better justice (15:2-6). They follow him into rebellion against their rightful leader, King David. Meanwhile, the legitimate leadership—David and his loyal commanders—ultimately prevails. The rightful king and his advisors (particularly Joab) make the strategically sound decisions, while the common people who followed Absalom are shown to have made the wrong choice by rebelling against their divinely-established king. The story validates the proper chain of authority and leadership while portraying the populace as having been deceived and led astray.
